mutants.description: Episode start leaves out the latch causes (inferred OVP and latch_assert), on the belief that a latch trip always follows a window trip that has already opened the episode
mutants.reason: An analog OVP trip while running, with nothing else recorded yet, sets fault_reg[4], but fault_time stays 0 instead of holding the trip time. Later causes cannot stamp it either, because the record is no longer empty.

mutants.description: Episode start leaves out the environmental causes (OTP and UVLO), as if only faults the converter itself causes could open an episode
mutants.reason: An OTP or UVLO that is the first cause while running sets its fault_reg bit, but fault_time stays 0. A later overcurrent in the same record does not stamp it, because the record is already non-empty.

mutants.description: Each soft-start retry is treated as a new episode: a cause captured during S_SS re-stamps fault_time even when the record already holds causes
mutants.reason: After an overcurrent in S_RUN is recorded, a restart that sees window_trip_SS (or any live cause in S_SS) overwrites fault_time with the time of the restart. The header says fault_time holds the start of the episode until the host reads it.

mutants.description: fault_time follows timestamp_ms whenever the record is empty and freezes once the first cause is captured, instead of being latched only at episode start
mutants.reason: After reset or after a host read with no cause live, fault_time reports the running ms count instead of 0. An empty record then shows a non-zero, changing start time.

mutants.description: The LATCH_ASSERT bit survives a host read and is made sticky until reset, like the CPLD's latch_assert, instead of being cleared with the rest of the record
mutants.reason: After a CPLD latch trip stops the converter, a host read should return fault_reg to 0 because the capture gate is closed. Under this mutant bit 3 stays set while the other bits and fault_time clear, so the next read still reports a latch trip with fault_time 0.
